`createTraitRegistry(...entries)` has the type signature accepting variadic `[string, Trait | Relation]` tuples.
contracts.adverse_condition: Verification requires type-checking usage authored from this contract's text alone, not adapted from the implementation's own tests.

contracts.text: `createTraitRegistry(...entries)` — each tuple's first element (the string) is used as the registry key for the trait or relation in the second element.
contracts.adverse_condition: Verification requires pairwise distinguishable inputs; a green test with only one entry or entries where key equals trait name cannot distinguish correct positional mapping from a swapped implementation.

contracts.text: `createTraitRegistry` throws an `Error` when two or more entries share the same string key.
contracts.adverse_condition: At least two entries have identical string keys but different trait/relation values.

contracts.text: `createTraitRegistry` throws an `Error` when the same `Trait` appears in two or more entries (duplicate traits).
contracts.adverse_condition: The same Trait reference or value is passed under at least two different keys.

contracts.text: `createTraitRegistry` throws an `Error` when the same `Relation` appears in two or more entries (duplicate relations).
contracts.adverse_condition: The same Relation reference or value is passed under at least two different keys.

contracts.text: `snapshotEntity(world, entity, registry)` has the type signature `(world: World, entity: Entity, registry: TraitRegistry) => EntitySnapshot`.
contracts.adverse_condition: Verification requires type-checking usage authored from this contract's text alone.

contracts.text: The returned `EntitySnapshot` has the shape `{ id: number, traits: Record<string, object | true>, relations?: Record<string, Array<{ targetId: number, data?: object }>> }`.
Tag traits (traits with no associated data) are stored as the literal value `true` in the snapshot's `traits` record.
contracts.adverse_condition: The entity possesses at least one data trait; testing with only tag traits cannot distinguish correct tag-trait handling from a bug that stores everything as `true` or everything as an object.

contracts.text: Data traits (traits with associated data) are stored as deep copies in the snapshot's `traits` record.
contracts.adverse_condition: The original trait data is mutated after the snapshot is captured; without post-snapshot mutation, a shallow copy or even a reference passes a green test.

contracts.text: Relations that have a store (carry data) include the `data` field as a deep copy in each element of the relation's array.
contracts.adverse_condition: The relation's data is mutated after the snapshot is captured; without post-snapshot mutation, a shallow copy passes.

contracts.text: The `relations` property is omitted entirely from the returned `EntitySnapshot` when the entity has no relations — the key must be absent, not present with an empty object or empty array.
contracts.adverse_condition: The entity has zero relations; an implementation that stores `relations: {}` or `relations: []` passes a truthiness or iteration check but violates the omission contract.

contracts.text: `snapshotEntity` throws an `Error` when the given entity has been destroyed.
contracts.adverse_condition: The entity argument refers to an entity that was destroyed before the call.

contracts.text: `snapshotEntity` throws an `Error` when the entity possesses a trait or relation whose key is not present in the given registry.
contracts.adverse_condition: The entity has a trait or relation that was not registered via `createTraitRegistry` (or an equivalent registry).

contracts.text: `snapshotWorld(world, registry)` has the type signature `(world: World, registry: TraitRegistry) => { entities: EntitySnapshot[] }`.
contracts.adverse_condition: Verification requires type-checking usage authored from this contract's text alone.

contracts.text: `snapshotWorld` returns an object with an `entities` array of `EntitySnapshot` objects.
`snapshotWorld` excludes the internal world entity from the returned `entities` array.
contracts.adverse_condition: The world contains at least one non-internal entity; testing with a world that only has the internal entity cannot prove exclusion vs. inclusion of that entity.

contracts.text: `rollbackEntity(world, entity, registry, snapshot)` has the type signature `(world: World, entity: Entity, registry: TraitRegistry, snapshot: EntitySnapshot) => void`.
contracts.adverse_condition: Verification requires type-checking usage authored from this contract's text alone.

contracts.text: `rollbackEntity` removes traits and relations the entity currently has that are not present in the snapshot — before adding or updating anything from the snapshot.
contracts.adverse_condition: The entity has at least one trait or relation not in the snapshot, and the snapshot also adds a trait with the same key but different data; adding first then removing would erase the just-added snapshot value.

contracts.text: After removal, `rollbackEntity` adds or updates traits and relations so the entity's state exactly matches the snapshot.
contracts.adverse_condition: The snapshot contains traits/relations that overlap keys with the entity's pre-rollback state; a partial update or add-without-update-semantics would leave stale data.

contracts.text: `rollbackEntity` throws an `Error` when a relation in the snapshot targets an entity ID that does not exist in the world.
contracts.adverse_condition: The snapshot contains a relation whose `targetId` does not correspond to any existing (non-destroyed) entity in the world at the time of rollback.

contracts.text: `rollbackEntity` throws an `Error` when the given entity has been destroyed.
contracts.adverse_condition: The entity argument refers to an entity that was destroyed before the call.

contracts.text: `rollbackEntity` throws an `Error` when the snapshot references a trait or relation key not present in the given registry.
contracts.adverse_condition: The snapshot's `traits` or `relations` contains a key that was never registered.

contracts.text: `rollbackWorld(world, registry, checkpoint)` has the type signature `(world: World, registry: TraitRegistry, checkpoint: { entities: EntitySnapshot[] }) => void`.
contracts.adverse_condition: Verification requires type-checking usage authored from this contract's text alone.

contracts.text: `rollbackWorld` fully replaces the existing world state — all current entities are destroyed or cleared before reapplying the checkpoint.
contracts.adverse_condition: The world contains entities not present in the checkpoint; if old entities survive the rollback, the replacement is not full.

contracts.text: `rollbackWorld` recreates entities using exactly the same numeric IDs as recorded in the checkpoint's entity snapshots.
contracts.adverse_condition: The checkpoint contains at least two entities with different IDs; testing with a single entity or all-new IDs cannot distinguish ID-preserving recreation from sequential reassignment.

contracts.text: `rollbackWorld` throws an `Error` when the checkpoint references a trait or relation key not present in the given registry.
contracts.adverse_condition: A snapshot in the checkpoint's `entities` array contains a trait or relation key absent from the registry.

contracts.text: `rollbackWorld` throws an `Error` for dangling relation targets — a relation in the checkpoint points to a target entity ID that does not exist among the checkpoint's own entities.
contracts.adverse_condition: A relation's `targetId` in one snapshot does not match the `id` of any snapshot in the same checkpoint's `entities` array.

contracts.text: `diffEntitySnapshots(a, b)` has the type signature `(a: EntitySnapshot, b: EntitySnapshot) => { addedTraits: string[], removedTraits: string[], changedTraits: string[] }`.
contracts.adverse_condition: Verification requires type-checking usage authored from this contract's text alone.

contracts.text: `diffEntitySnapshots` returns an object with exactly the three array properties `addedTraits`, `removedTraits`, and `changedTraits`.
`diffEntitySnapshots` — `addedTraits` contains trait keys present in `b.traits` but absent in `a.traits`.
contracts.adverse_condition: Verification requires asymmetric inputs where `b` has traits not in `a`; symmetric or identical snapshots produce empty arrays and cannot distinguish added vs. removed.

contracts.text: `diffEntitySnapshots` — `removedTraits` contains trait keys present in `a.traits` but absent in `b.traits`.
contracts.adverse_condition: Verification requires asymmetric inputs where `a` has traits not in `b`.

contracts.text: `diffEntitySnapshots` — `changedTraits` contains trait keys present in both `a.traits` and `b.traits` but whose values differ by shallow equality.
contracts.adverse_condition: Verification requires a trait present in both snapshots with different shallow values; identical values or deep-only differences incorrectly produce an empty `changedTraits` array.

contracts.text: All three arrays (`addedTraits`, `removedTraits`, `changedTraits`) are sorted in ascending alphabetical order.
contracts.adverse_condition: Two or more entries exist in any category; a single-entry array is trivially sorted and cannot prove the sort implementation.

contracts.text: Data comparison for trait values uses shallow equality (e.g., `===` or equivalent), not deep equality.
contracts.adverse_condition: Two trait values are different object instances with identical deep contents; deep equality would report them as unchanged, shallow equality must report them as changed.

contracts.text: `diffEntitySnapshots` throws an `Error` when either `a` or `b` is `null`.
contracts.adverse_condition: Argument `a` is `null` (and `b` is valid), or `b` is `null` (and `a` is valid), or both are `null`.

contracts.text: `diffEntitySnapshots` throws an `Error` when either `a` or `b` is `undefined`.
contracts.adverse_condition: Argument `a` is `undefined` (and `b` is valid), or `b` is `undefined` (and `a` is valid), or both are `undefined`.

contracts.text: `diffWorldSnapshots(before, after)` has the type signature `(before: { entities: EntitySnapshot[] }, after: { entities: EntitySnapshot[] }) => { added: number[], removed: number[], changed: number[] }`.
contracts.adverse_condition: Verification requires type-checking usage authored from this contract's text alone.

contracts.text: `diffWorldSnapshots` returns an object with exactly the three array properties `added`, `removed`, and `changed`.
`diffWorldSnapshots` — `added` contains the `id` values of entities present in `after.entities` but absent from `before.entities`.
contracts.adverse_condition: Verification requires asymmetric inputs where `after` has entity IDs not in `before`.

contracts.text: `diffWorldSnapshots` — `removed` contains the `id` values of entities present in `before.entities` but absent from `after.entities`.
contracts.adverse_condition: Verification requires asymmetric inputs where `before` has entity IDs not in `after`.

contracts.text: `diffWorldSnapshots` — `changed` contains the `id` values of entities present in both snapshots whose trait/relation data differs (by the equality rules below).
contracts.adverse_condition: An entity exists in both snapshots with identical ID but different trait values; identical snapshots produce empty `changed` and cannot prove detection.

contracts.text: All three arrays (`added`, `removed`, `changed`) are sorted in ascending numeric order.
contracts.adverse_condition: Two or more entity IDs exist in any category; a single-entry array is trivially sorted.

contracts.text: Trait key ordering within an entity snapshot does not affect equality — `{ traits: { a: true, b: true } }` is equal to `{ traits: { b: true, a: true } }`.
contracts.adverse_condition: Two snapshots of the same entity have identical traits but with keys inserted in different order; key iteration order must be normalized or ignored during comparison.

contracts.text: Relation key ordering within an entity snapshot does not affect equality — different insertion orders of relation keys are treated as equal.
contracts.adverse_condition: Two snapshots have the same relations but with keys in different insertion order.

contracts.text: Relation target ordering within a single relation's array does not affect equality — `[{ targetId: 1 }, { targetId: 2 }]` is equal to `[{ targetId: 2 }, { targetId: 1 }]`.
contracts.adverse_condition: A relation's target array has the same elements in different order; element order must be normalized or ignored.

contracts.text: Trait and relation data within world-level diffing is compared using shallow equality.
contracts.adverse_condition: Two trait values are different object instances with identical deep contents; deep equality would report them as unchanged, shallow equality must report them as changed.

contracts.text: An entity snapshot with `relations: {}` (empty object) is treated as equivalent to an entity snapshot that has no `relations` key at all.
contracts.adverse_condition: One snapshot omits `relations` while the other has `relations: {}`; a strict key-presence check would incorrectly report them as different.

contracts.text: `diffWorldSnapshots` throws an `Error` if either `before` or `after` is `null`.
contracts.adverse_condition: Argument `before` is `null` (and `after` is valid), or `after` is `null` (and `before` is valid), or both are `null`.

contracts.text: `diffWorldSnapshots` throws an `Error` if either `before` or `after` is `undefined`.
contracts.adverse_condition: Argument `before` is `undefined` (and `after` is valid), or `after` is `undefined` (and `before` is valid), or both are `undefined`.

contracts.text: `diffWorldSnapshots` throws an `Error` if either `before` or `after` lacks an `entities` array property.
contracts.adverse_condition: One argument is a plain object without an `entities` key, or has `entities` set to a non-array value.
